records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy alloy (HEA) superconductors be utilized stably under extreme conditions?. System: Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–Ti high-entropy alloy. Processing: pulsed laser deposition (PLD) with substrate temperatures ranging from 270 to 620 °C. Test conditions: various magnetic fields, ion irradiation with 200 keV Kr ions. Findings: High critical current density (Jc) of >1 MA cm−2 at 4.2 K; Robust superconductivity against irradiation-induced disorder; Jc values over 1000 times more resistant to displacement damage than other superconductors; High Tc of 7.28 K for the film deposited at 520 °C; Strong vortex pinning strength. Mechanism: The high atomic-level stress and/or high-level lattice distortion in HEAs resulting from their high configuration entropy may contribute to the robust superconductivity against irradiation damage. Quote: "HEA superconductors have considerable potential for use under extreme conditions"
